stem: Which paediatric chest feature helps explain why loss of lung volume is a concern during suspected anaphylaxis?

options.text: Compliant chest wall with less support for maintenance of lung volume
Rigid chest wall with improved support for lung volume
Lower airway resistance because of wider airways
Reduced ventilation-perfusion mismatch because of greater alveolar reserve

explanation: Compliant chest wall with less support for maintenance of lung volume is correct because children have a more compliant chest wall, so they have less support for maintaining lung volume and can decompensate more easily with respiratory compromise.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

optionExplanations.A: Correct because a compliant paediatric chest wall provides less support for maintaining lung volume.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because children do not have a rigid chest wall that improves support for lung volume; the chest wall is more compliant.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because children have fewer alveoli than adults, not more.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because smaller paediatric airways increase resistance rather than lowering it.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because children are more prone to ventilation-perfusion mismatch, not reduced mismatch from greater alveolar reserve.
